URL: (compiled) Thursday 15 October 2026 MORNING ticker basis
Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 08:51 BST. Cross-check: Trading Economics (UK 10Y, US 10Y, WTI, GB100).
NOTE ON TIMING: this edition is late because the scheduled job hung for 53 minutes without producing an
edition and was killed at 08:49. The read is therefore nearly an hour after the London open rather than
before it — which, for once, means the FTSE is LIVE rather than lagged.

*** A RISK-OFF MORNING, AND THE FTSE IS THE ODD ONE OUT AGAIN ***
Every classic risk-off signal is firing at once: equities down in Asia and on Wall Street, government
bonds rallying hard, gold bid, oil sold, volatility up.
  Gilt   5.3415, about 8bp lower   | UST 5.089, about 10bp lower | US30Y 5.435, about 9bp lower
  Gold   4,141.33 +0.88            | VIX 17.44 +3.38            | Brent 104.00 -1.94
The cause is the global artificial-intelligence sell-off that deepened overnight, with a trading halt on
South Korea's Kospi and the Nikkei 225 down about 5%. That is the world column's lead.
AND YET THE FTSE IS UP, at 10,754.52 and +0.28% at 08:35, a second consecutive session in which London
has risen on a day the rest of the world fell. Worth stating rather than smoothing: the index is heavy in
energy, defence and banks and light in technology, so an AI-led rout hurts it least.

*** THE FTSE FEED IS LIVE — BECAUSE WE ARE LATE ***
The feed lag that has defeated every pre-09:00 reading this week is absent at 08:51. .FTSE returned
10,754.52 stamped 08:35, a genuine intraday price. This is the first morning edition in eight days to
carry a live FTSE, and the only reason is that the hang pushed publication past the lag window. Trading
Economics gives GB100 at 10,772.15 +0.44% — about 18 points higher on a slightly later read, which is
normal provider drift on a moving index rather than a disagreement.

*** GILT: THE WIDEST THREE-WAY SPREAD THIS WEEK ***
  CNBC:              5.3415, change -0.0887 (prev 5.4302)  -> -0.09
  Trading Economics: 5.34,   day change -0.060              -> -0.06
  Our own series:    5.34 against last night's published 5.42 -> -0.08
PUBLISHED: 5.34, -0.08 — our own series, sitting between the two providers, which is how this has been
handled all week when they disagree. The spread is 3bp, wider than any day since Monday, and on a morning
when the gilt is moving this fast a provider's snapshot time matters more than usual. All three agree on
the level to two decimals and on the direction; only the size is disputed.

*** TWO INSTRUMENTS WHERE LAST NIGHT'S FIGURE WAS AN INTRADAY READ, NOT A CLOSE ***
Last night's edition was published at 18:10 and read live at 18:06, while Wall Street was still open. The
settled closes came in lower:
  UST  published 5.23 intraday -> actual close 5.19 -> now 5.089, so -0.10 on the close, not -0.14
  VIX  published 16.54 intraday -> actual close 16.87
  Brent published 106.58 intraday -> actual settle 106.06
Neither is an error in last night's edition; an intraday read and a close are different things. But the
change figures this morning are computed against the CLOSES, which is the only consistent basis.
S&P 500 carries Wednesday's close of 7,718.94, down 1.11%, with Wall Street shut until 14:30 BST.

BRENT CROSS-CHECK: CNBC 104.00 -1.94% against Trading Economics WTI at 94.13 -1.01%. Different contracts,
same direction. Oil falling on a risk-off day, with the Gulf quiet overnight, is consistent.
